scopeBoundary: Public dashboard static interface only. Do not hash status files, credential endpoints, owner worktrees or entire Git tree.
dependencyFact: architecture.js imports only ./architecture-data.js among these examined modules; app.js and local-access.js have no static import declarations.
candidate: A bounded immutable asset bundle per server instance can provide one coherent derived UI revision without re-reading Git or every asset on each author-data poll.
coherence: Read and hash the exact existing public allowlist once before serving, enforce a finite aggregate size cap, and serve those same captured bytes for the lifetime of that instance.
Derive revision from sorted route/bytes/digest tuples of source assets. A substituted HTML version marker must be excluded from its own derivation to avoid a self-referential hash.
Expose the loaded revision in the served HTML and the currently serving revision through the existing bounded summary response or header; compare only when both are present.
No inline script or weakened Content-Security-Policy. Use existing app.js to read the marker and render the explicit update action.

This deliberately makes asset changes require the already-controlled server restart. An owner must choose and document this lifecycle rather than claiming disk hot editing and immutable serving simultaneously.
userBehavior: Keep author facts refreshing and mark interface-update availability separately.
Never auto-reload or close selected task/review or expanded claim. The user chooses the update action.
Keep display of unknown client version honest; old pre-feature loaded code will not gain a notifier retroactively and needs an ordinary reload once.
Metadata/status-only commits must not create new interface-update prompts.
validation: Two immutable versions A/B with same registry/status facts: loaded A receives B response and displays update action without losing selection or data refresh.
Identical static assets with changed status facts or commit metadata produce no update notice.
Missing/unknown version does not claim current or fabricate stale.
When on-disk assets change after startup, same instance serves its captured coherent bytes; new instance changes revision and bytes together.
Malicious or oversized unexpected asset input fails in bounded startup path; no runtime registry crawl.
Keyboard-accessible update action and focus/selection continuity require mounted browser verification; pure hashes alone do not prove it.
costEvidence: The fixed eight allowlisted source files total126100B; this is input size, not measured runtime memory or latency. A bounded in-memory static representation looks feasible but has not been benchmarked.
coordination: Existing D05/dashboard-followup owner scopes any implementation, exact claim and controlled deployment. No second registry or editable state source.
cleanCode: Keep one asset identity and one clear per-instance asset lifetime; prefer reusing summary delivery over introducing a polling subsystem.
